AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2, copied verbatim as that section binds every batch. The sim has no add-to-room phase - creature creation IS construction - so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (phantasmal_gardener.py:39-50). Same observable today, established by execution rather than assumed, on all three clauses: (a) listener set - the only ported listeners on the hooks a starting power can reach are relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (modify_power_amount) and relics/vambrace.py:26-40 / relics/paels_legion.py:36-43 (modify_block_multiplicative); all four gate on target is self.player / applier is self.player / card is not None, and a monster's starting power is self-applied with no card, so none of them can fire; sts2_rl/potions.py implements none of the four hooks. (b) HP-roll inversion - the sim applies the power before the Niche roll and the game after it; of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp at all and only inside revive() (powers.py:1581), never at apply time. (c) roll ordering - MachineMonster.__init__ rolls the first move (state_machine.py:301) before the subclass applies its powers, but `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` shows all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-op: every initial state is a MoveState, so monster_state_machine step 30's early return fires and the first roll evaluates no branch and reads no power. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic, potion or power listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. RULE 7 NOTE: that rationale cites four relic files and powers.py which this record does NOT hash, exactly as the seam records disclose. Payload matches: PowerCmd.Apply<SkittishPower>(..., Creature, SkittishAmount, Creature, null) with SkittishAmount 6 non-ascension (PhantasmalGardener.cs:49, 89-93) vs PowerCmd.apply(hooks, self, SkittishPower, 6) (phantasmal_gardener.py:50). Clause (c) needs care for this unit because its initial state is a ConditionalBranchState, NOT a MoveState - so monster_state_machine step 30's sticky early return does not fire and the first roll really does walk the branch. It is still harmless: the branch's four predicates read `self.slot` (phantasmal_gardener.py:65-68), a plain string set at :46 before super().__init__, and not a power - so the roll cannot observe the not-yet-applied SkittishPower. Executed (monster_probes_b03.py graphs): the default slot 'first' yields initial=FLAIL_MOVE, log=['FLAIL_MOVE'], telegraph=FLAIL_MOVE - the branch resolved, was not logged, and drew nothing.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: PhantasmalGardener.cs:95-116 vs phantasmal_gardener.py:52-73. Chain BITE -> LASH -> FLAIL -> ENLARGE -> BITE on both sides; initial state is the ConditionalBranchState 'INIT_MOVE'; the four AddState calls are in the same ORDER with the same predicates - (:103) FLAIL if SlotName == 'first', (:104) BITE if 'second', (:105) LASH if 'third', (:106) ENLARGE if 'fourth' -> (py :65-68) the same four against self.slot. Order is observable (ConditionalBranchState returns the FIRST true branch, monster_state_machine step 26) even though the four predicates happen to be mutually exclusive. The slot strings themselves match PhantasmalGardenersElite.Slots = [first, second, third, fourth] (PhantasmalGardenersElite.cs:18) and the sim's _SLOTS tuple (phantasmal_gardener.py:26), and the encounter hands them out in the same order (PhantasmalGardenersElite.cs:33-45 vs phantasmal_gardener.py:96-97), so gardener i enters the cycle at the same point. Intents: SingleAttackIntent(5)/(7), MultiAttackIntent(1,3), BuffIntent. No RandomBranchState, so PROMPT.md class 6 cannot apply and no roll draws.

guards.what: The four gardeners' slot assignment and list order
guards.rationale: Checked directly because the sibling unit monster/living_fog has a LIVE gap on exactly this mechanism. Here the encounter's GenerateMonsters emits the four in Slots order (first, second, third, fourth - PhantasmalGardenersElite.cs:33-45), so CombatState.SortEnemiesBySlotName (CombatState.cs:495-501, called from CombatManager.cs:846-851) is a no-op, and the sim's create_monsters builds them in the same order (phantasmal_gardener.py:96-97). No mid-combat spawn exists for this encounter, so the ordering divergence living_fog exhibits cannot arise. Recorded so the two records' different verdicts on 'slot placement' are visibly about two different encounters (rule 3, and PROMPT.md class 29 - do not copy a sibling's verdict).

All 29 PROMPT.md bug classes checked against this unit. Class 6: no RandomBranchState. Class 10: EnlargeTriggers/CurrentScale are per-combat and presentation; the sim rebuilds the monster per combat anyway. Class 21: neither kills nor is retained. Class 29 (siblings may differ on purpose): answered in the slot guard above.
